text.p: Here are highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:

- Nearly 13,000 students received "Maturitaets" diplomas in Switzerland last year, six percent fewer than in 1994, according to the Federal Department of Statistics. The diplomas allow students to begin university studies.

- The British newspaper "Daily Telegraph" reported that Nazis brought art treasures worth between three and 15 billion pounds belonging to Jews into Switzerland during World War Two. - Citizens of St Gallen voted at the weekend in favour of privatising the St Gallen Cantonal Bank.

- Hundreds of people gathered at Zurich's Muensterhof Square in the old town on Friday to comemmorate the 50th anniversary of Winston Churchill's visit. The main speaker, former German chancellor Helmut Schmidt, urged Switzerland not to wait much longer to join Europe.
- SGS, a goods and service inspection firm operating worldwide, increased net profit by 10.9 percent to 110.9 million Swiss francs in the first six months of 1996.
- The Swiss postal service is planning to sell insurance over the counter. So far 12 insurance companies are interested in cooperating.

- The Canton of Zurich is cutting salaries of most of its 44,000 civil employees by three percent. None will receive any pay raise to compensate for inflation from now until 1999. - Rainer E. Gut, Credit Suisse's chairman of the board, said he will make the bank number one among Swiss banks in terms of profit.
- A referendum calling for increased tax on capital gains was voted down in the canton of Neuchatel at the weekend.
